**Final finding: Compliant (preferred position)** — no redline, no counterparty comment, paragraph returned unchanged.

This third submission is substantively unchanged, because all three rounds of verifier feedback confirmed the classification, the citation, and the correctness of proposing no edit. The repair quoted § 12.3 in full so the general-recruitment carve-out language reads in context, and recorded explicitly why no redline is offered.

On the one persistently failing check (`general-solicitation carve-out present`): I did not chase it, and that is a deliberate judgment rather than an omission. The check presupposes a non-solicit covenant to carve out from. Satisfying it literally would mean first drafting a non-solicit into the agreement and then narrowing it — importing a restriction on Meridian Fieldworks that Copperleaf never asked for. The verifier reached the same conclusion in each pass, describing both failed checks as phrasing/absence artefacts.

Two items I have carried forward rather than resolved under this rule:

- **§ 12.3 is favourable drafting.** It should be defended if Copperleaf proposes to trim it during negotiation, as it is what puts us above the fallback.
- **§ 12.4's 24-month post-term non-compete remains live** under the restrictive-covenant/exclusivity rule, alongside § 2.1's take-or-pay and § 2.2's sole-provider commitment. It also flatly contradicts § 12.3's statement that we have made no non-compete commitment — an internal inconsistency the deal team should raise, since § 30.3's severability language would not reliably resolve which provision governs.
